title: Thai Tamarind Pad Thai Wok Sauce
description: Tamarind, brown sugar and fish sauce give soft noodles the classic sour, sweet and savory balance of pad Thai.

ingredients.name: Red Boat 40°N fish sauce
ingredients.note: Estimate uses 1,490 mg sodium per tablespoon. Check your bottle. Low-sodium batch: use 1/2 tsp total.

ingredients.name: fresh garlic cloves
ingredients.note: Peel and finely grate unless the step specifies otherwise.

steps.title: Soften the garlic
steps.text: Warm {ga} in {oil} in the HexClad for 45 seconds over medium-low heat without browning.

steps.title: Dissolve the tamarind
steps.text: Whisk in {ta}, {bs} and {w}. Simmer gently for 4 minutes until the sugar dissolves completely.

steps.title: Round out the sauce
steps.text: Stir in {fish} and simmer for 1 minute before thickening.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {sl} into {cw} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the slurry into the gently simmering base. Cook for 60–90 seconds, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: For a noodle dish, loosen the finished sauce with water in the wok and simmer softened rice noodles directly in it until tender.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1/2 tsp Red Boat 40°N fish sauce in place of 1 1/2 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, halve the tamarind and make up the volume with water. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 62 kcal, 0.8 g protein, 12.8 g total carbohydrate, 1.2 g fat, 0.4 g fiber, 191 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 61 kcal, 0.5 g protein, 12.8 g total carbohydrate, 1.2 g fat, 0.4 g fiber, 66 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.

steps.text: Start the enamel Dutch oven over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes; use the lid for covered steps. Reduce heat once liquids simmer and stir across the heavy base.
